assets.sceneAlt: Sun Over the Forest by Markus Naarttijärvi: olive corner sofa, oak coffee table, drinks and a striped throw beneath a sunset photograph on a peach wall.
assets.reviewStatus: Preview candidate; not approved for publication
assets.prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural. Create ONE tall portrait 4:5 editorial DSLR interior photograph for Scandinavian Art. Reference 1 is the exact original Sun Over the Forest photographic artwork; reference 2 is a LABELLED catalogue item and material board. Use the board's selected products, floor material and paint swatch only; never copy any whole room or furniture in a floor/paint photo. No other art or furniture.

The framed print is a physically real 70 × 50 cm landscape paper print in a thin natural oak glazed frame about 72 × 52 cm, hanging above and related to the occupied sofa seating group. The full source image is 4:3 landscape; show ALL four edges and original composition inside the white paper, with appropriate white margins, wider at the sides. Do not crop, stretch, invent a different sunset or turn it into an illuminated screen. Original photograph: gigantic distinct white-hot circular sun slightly above centre, horizontal cloud bands crossing its lower half, orange and rust sky, silhouettes of conifer treetops along the lower third, nearly black forest base. The sun belongs only INSIDE the framed photograph and casts NO light into the room. The paper, ink, glass, oak frame and neighbouring peach wall all receive the same actual LEFT window daylight falloff. A soft, physically plausible left-window reflection crosses a small part of the glazing without obscuring the sun; real recessed glass edge and a frame contact shadow consistent with the room. Render the art as part of initial image generation, never composite it afterwards.

Scene: a lived-in family sitting room. The EXACT catalogue olive-green IKEA corner sectional, 310 cm wide and 71 cm tall, rests against the peach-painted wall. The framed print is only 72/310 = 23% of that true sofa width. Do not inflate the print to fill the wall, but frame closely enough for it to remain clear. The EXACT catalogue natural-oak Nyhem coffee table, 89 × 59 × 37 cm, sits in reachable position in front of the sofa, its feet on the catalogue Crayon beige/multicolour 170 × 240 cm rug. The Marimekko powder/off-white Jokeri cushion is gently compressed in the corner, and the black-and-white Tekla striped wool throw is casually draped over one sofa arm. The clear Ripple carafe is filled with water and paired with two HAY clear drinking glasses on the coffee table, within reach of the seats; one book can be in use near a glass. Keep useful surface visible. No extra sofa, chair, sideboard, shelving or lamps.

Use the catalogue Peach wall colour alone, not its pictured console. Exposed floor is the catalogue Oak wood flooring with broad pale timber boards and plausible room-scale plank joints, not parquet. A real window at the LEFT edge is the sole daylight source. Softly broken daylight lights part of wall and floor, with sheltered sofa folds darker. A standing camera around 145 cm, level verticals, moderate 40–50 mm view, slight oblique viewpoint showing tabletop and seating without an oversized foreground corner. Carefully developed low-ISO full-frame DSLR RAW character: restrained exposure, neutral daylight balance, local volume, organic but clean materials, real contact shadows, readable print, moderate depth of field. Avoid flat HDR illumination, CGI perfection, generic vase props, artificial grain, logos, people and text.

qa.art: Recognisable source composition and dark lower forest; rendered sun remains inside print.
qa.integration: Good left-window reflection, frame shadow and shared directional light.
qa.scale: Frame looks a little generous against full 310 cm sofa, whose right portion is cropped; precise width ratio cannot be confirmed.
qa.products: Sofa, Nyhem table, Crayon rug, cushion, throw, carafe and glasses visible.
qa.room: Natural seating activity and credible floor/window geometry.
